transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-09 08:00 PT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Alvarez (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (NimbleCare ML Eng), James Ortiz (Head of Platform), Oliver Reed (Security), Priya Nair (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough)
- Today: triage model candidates, confirm pin policy, do a dry-run 'unpin' tabletop.
- Roadblocks: a couple of prompts show hallucination/regression on smaller quantized variants; KV cache behavior differs from dev load.
- Immediate asks: bench sweep, pricing tiers, security docs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we wanted to keep this tight — triage the model list and run a quick tabletop for emergency unpin, is that still the plan?
[00:10] Maya: yep that's great, we got a few prompts that regressed on the smaller q models so want to lock decisions today ideally.
[00:18] James: timeline wise we've got exec review next Thursday so any change needs a safe rollback plan.
[00:25] Ethan: ok good context. quick housekeeping — we've got the catalog comparisons in the shared drive, i'll pull up the three finalists: redwood-llm-3-small, rdx-gpt-3.5-q4, and a tuned open-llama variant.
[00:40] Priya: can you use the customer-friendly names in the sheet? the team keeps getting confused between rdx-gpt vs redwood-llm.
[00:48] Ethan: noted, i'll add a mapping.
[00:52] Maya: first thing — latency. under our P95 SLA we need < 320ms on gen calls at median payload. the small q model hits cost but spikes at p95 under our tail.
[01:05] Ethan: yeah the quantized path trades accuracy for throughput; we've seen the same in the pilot. one trick is KV prefix caching — if you can warm the cache for common prefixes, p95 drops a bunch. but with your distribution and cold starts it may not be reliable.
[01:26] Oliver: quick security flag — audit logs retention, SSO/SAML, and KMS vendor we'll need those to sign off. also, do you provide per-token redaction logs?
[01:36] Sofia: for SOC2 customers we have audit logs and KMS integration; we'll share the docs. per-token redaction is not native but we support structured logging and can annotate requests with redaction metadata.
[01:51] James: perfect, please send.
[01:55] Ethan: back to model behavior — the tuned open-llama did well on your dev set for recall on legacy prompts but had a higher latency variance. rdx-gpt-3.5-q4 is cost-efficient but we observed a subtle coherence drop on multi-turns in a couple of prompts.
[02:16] Maya: those coherence drops are the ones we care about — they impact downstream scoring. any way to detect and route those cases to a stronger model automatically?
[02:27] Ethan: yes, you can use a lightweight reranker or simple heuristic: if the next-turn probability drops below threshold, route to a stronger model or use a soft fallback. Redwood supports route-by-policy — latency/cost/region.
[02:40] Priya: soft fallback meaning shadowing stronger model or full request re-issue?
[02:46] Ethan: can be either. shadowing is cheaper for monitoring; re-issue gives immediate correct response but adds latency. you can also do speculative execution in some cases.
[02:57] Sofia: ok so we have functional fallbacks. today's critical piece is pin policy — do we hard-pin to redwood-llm-3-small for cost, or soft-pin with automatic fallback to redwood-llm-3-full?
[03:12] Maya: we prefer soft-pin, but need hard unpin runbook — in case the pinned model causes a regression at scale.
[03:20] James: agree — and we need an emergency cutoff that doesn't require ops in the middle of the night.
[03:27] Ethan: that's where 'unpin via policy' with a flag and immediate region-wide fallback helps. we recommend a canary window: 5% traffic to new pin, monitor evals and latency, then roll. for emergency unpin we have a pre-baked override that re-routes to fallback model.
[03:46] Oliver: how fast does that override propagate? if we flip at 2am, will it take 90s or 10s?
[03:52] Ethan: typical propagation is sub-30s for control-plane flags; token-level caching and KV might mean some in-flight requests still hit old variant for a short window — so we call it eventual but near-instant.
[04:06] Maya: that's acceptable but we should rehearse the edge cases. can we do a tabletop?
[04:10] Sofia: yes — propose a 30-min tabletop next week where we simulate a bad regression and walk through the unpin steps.
[04:18] James: sounds good. target 2026-04-16 10:00 PT?
[04:22] Sofia: i'll propose that.
[04:24] Ethan: quick note on metrics — for the bench sweep i'll capture median/p95/p99 latency, tokens-per-second, and per-token cost estimate across seq lengths 64/256/1024 to mirror your traffic.
[04:37] Maya: please include the prompt-level regression flag examples so we can see false positives on reranker.
[04:44] Ethan: got it.
[04:46] Priya: pricing — we need to see Dedicated sizing; we might want reserved capacity for predictable throughput.
[04:53] Sofia: we'll send a tiered pricing doc: hosted pilot, dedicated small, dedicated medium; shows commit levels and burst options.
[05:01] Maya: one more tech question — we noticed KV-cache invalidation behaves differently in your sandbox vs our staging cluster. cache misses are higher under a multi-tenant noise pattern.
[05:12] Ethan: yes that's because sandbox warmers use deterministic prefixes; with real traffic the cache churn increases. for your workload we may suggest prefix-based caching and slightly higher batch windows to increase hit rate if latency SLO permits.
[05:26] Oliver: any compliance issues with prefix caching? does it retain sensitive prefixes?
[05:31] Sofia: caching is memory-only on the runtime and not persisted to disk; we can scope what is cached and apply request-level redaction before caching. we'll document this in the security packet.
[05:45] James: ok good.
[05:47] Ethan: about regressions on the smaller quantized variants — we've instrumented a lightweight classifier you can run post-response to detect hallucination patterns; if it triggers, route to solver model. but that classifier has some FPR so we'll need to tune it against your sample prompts.
[06:05] Maya: acceptable if we can see the false-positive rates.
[06:09] Sofia: action items we'll capture in the notes and i'll email the pilot pricing + runbook draft.
[06:15] Priya: can we also get a one-page decision matrix: cost vs latency vs quality for the three finalists? that'll help product decide in the exec meeting.
[06:24] Sofia: absolutely — ethan will produce that and attach the heatmap.
[06:28] James: last thing — vendors. the security team asked if you work with any third-party inference caching layers; we've been evaluating a self-hosted redis-backed approach. how does that interplay?
[06:40] Ethan: you can front the runtime with redis for your own prefix-level cache but we'd need to ensure TTLs and redaction rules align. Redwood's built-in KV is optimized for model semantics, but external cache can work with some integration work.
[06:55] Oliver: ok we'll share our redis configs.
[06:57] Sofia: great. let's confirm next steps and tabletop time. thanks all.
[07:05] (end)
